subject: Post-call: Medify procurement checklist + approval asks
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Sullivan <anna.sullivan@medifyhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 20:10:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call: Medify procurement checklist + approval asks

Anna — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we all have alignment.

Summary (30‑min call)
- Use case: Medify wants to run a patient-conversation summarization pilot across 3 clinical teams (~1000 sessions/month).
- Requirements called out: encrypted at-rest + in-transit, SOC2 evidence, 12-month data retention policy, SLA: 99.9% monthly uptime, and per-session PII redaction knobs.
- Timeline: pilot kickoff target May 4, 2‑month pilot, then decision by July execs.

Open asks you flagged:
1) Procurement wants a redline-ready MSA and a short answers RFI (security/compliance).
2) Procurement is sensitive to any SLA deviations or price concessions tied to pilot success metrics.
3) IT security (Kevin) may request a short security exception if we suggest token-level logging for debugging.

What I promised to send
- Attached: Medify_RFI_answers.pdf (answered by our security team).
- Attached: Draft_MSA_redline.docx — initial commercial + SLA variant we discussed.
- SLA_variance_request.pdf — one‑page note explaining requested SLA tweaks for pilot.

Internal asks (cc’d):
- Ben: can we confirm pilot commercial (one-time onboarding credit + pilot discount) and approve the pricing outline in the draft MSA?
- Laura: please review the redline and confirm if the SLA variance & indemnity language are acceptable or need escalation.
- Dev: review the RFI answers and flag any items that require a security exception (esp. token logging and KV cache debugging).

Next external steps
- Anna / Kevin: if the RFI + draft MSA look directionally ok, propose DocuSign-ready MSA and target signature by Apr 30 to keep May 4 kickoff.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a short internal thread in case we need approvals routed.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0198
attachments: Medify_RFI_answers.pdf, Draft_MSA_redline.docx, SLA_variance_request.pdf
From: Anna Sullivan <anna.sullivan@medifyhealth.com>

Cc: Kevin Moriarty <kevin.moriarty@medifyhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 02:35:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: Medify procurement checklist + approval asks

Tessa — appreciate the quick follow. Initial read looks promising. A few follow-ups from procurement/IT: 

Procurement (my side):
- Pricing: we need a short commercial summary (line items + pilot credit) that we can share with finance. Can Ben send a one‑pager?
- MSA: our legal will want to see the redline; please ask counsel to keep the limitation of liability section within our standard band — any larger deviation will require exec approval.

IT/security (Kevin):
- RFI: thanks for the doc. Kevin flagged question 8 (token storage) — if you need to enable any session-level logs for debugging, we need a formal exception request with mitigation and retention window.
- Encryption: confirm KMS integration (we prefer customer-managed keys).

Timeline: can you get the commercial one‑pager and DocuSign‑ready MSA to us by Apr 20? That gives our teams time to review before the requested May 4 start.

Thanks,
Anna Sullivan
Director, Procurement — Medify Health
anna.sullivan@medifyhealth.com
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2026 14:05:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: Medify procurement checklist + approval asks — internal approval routing

Team — forwarding Anna’s reply and the attachments. This is the internal approvals lane so I can keep the external thread clean. TL;DR asks: commercial one‑pager & approval for pilot discount; legal signoff on MSA redline and SLA variance; security signoff or formal exception process for token logging/KMS.

Commercial ask (Ben):
- Proposal outline in draft_MSA: 2‑month pilot, $7,500 pilot credit toward first paid month, 30% pilot discount on list rates during pilot, auto-convert to paid at agreed token tiers unless we opt out. Need your note to attach to the MSA for procurement.

Legal ask (Laura):
- Please review Draft_MSA_redline.docx. The specific points I flagged inline: SLA variance (we proposed 99.9% vs Medify’s 99.95%), limitation of liability cap aligned to monthly fees (they may push for higher), and data retention language (they want 12 months).

Security ask (Dev):
- RFI answers are high-level. Kevin asked for KMS details and a formal exception for token/session logs if needed. If we recommend customer-managed keys, do we have any operational blockers for the pilot? If an exception is necessary, please outline mitigations and a retention limit.

If we can get green lights from each of you by EOD Wed (Apr 14), I’ll share a one‑pager and updated DocuSign draft to Anna on Thu.

Thanks — Tessa

Tessa — OK to proceed commercially. Approve the pilot pricing outline as described (one-time onboarding credit + 30% pilot discount). I’ll draft the one‑pager and share it to the drive link you provided.

Notes:
- If legal needs a concession to SLA in exchange for a longer term commitment, i’m ok to include a conditional clause (e.g., extended term + credit) but prefer to avoid changing core indemnities.

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2026 10:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call: Medify procurement checklist + approval asks — internal approval routing

Thanks — I reviewed the draft and here are the items I need to resolve before we send anything externally: 

1) SLA variance: 99.9% for a pilot is acceptable, but we must add a rollback plan and credit table tied to monthly uptime buckets. I’ll prepare the table and insert it into the redline.
2) Limitation of liability: we must keep the cap standard (12 months fees) unless there is an exec exception. If Medify pushes higher, we’ll need a signed escalation to Legal/Finance.
3) Data retention: 12 months is fine if paired with customer-managed KMS for the pilot; confirm Dev that we can enable CMK for the May start.
4) Token logging: if Dev requests an exception, I need the mitigation plan (short retention window, restricted ACLs, and audit log export).

Action items:
- Dev: please confirm KMS CMK feasibility and whether token logging can be replaced by a debug mode that avoids PII capture. If not, prepare the exception request bullets.
- Tessa: I’ll send back an annotated Draft_MSA_redline.docx with the SLA credit table and required language by EOD.

Laura Bennett
Legal Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
